seo.title: Bathroom Survey in Maidenhead | £125 Fixed-Price Survey | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: Book a £125 bathroom survey in Maidenhead. We measure, check waste runs and access, and scope everything from riverside houses to town-centre apartments before any quote.

hero.intro: Before we quote for a bathroom installation anywhere in Maidenhead, we carry out a fixed-price £125 survey at the property. It's the stage where a floor plan on paper meets the reality of your walls, your waste runs and your access routes, and it's what stops a quote turning into a list of surprises once the fitting team is on site. Maidenhead is one of the more varied towns we survey in, precisely because its position on the Thames has shaped the housing in two quite different directions. Along and near the river you'll find larger detached properties, some period, some built more recently, generally on generous plots that give more freedom over bathroom layout than a terraced property allows. Away from the riverside, the town has a substantial core of Victorian and Edwardian housing, alongside extensive post-war and modern suburban development and newer town-centre apartment schemes. That range means we never assume what a survey will find before we've actually measured the room — a Maidenhead address tells us very little on its own about what's underneath the floor or behind the wall.

sections.heading: What the £125 survey covers
sections.body: The survey fee is fixed at £125 regardless of the size or complexity of the room, and it's deducted from your project cost if you go ahead with an installation. On the day, we measure the room accurately, identify where the waste pipe currently runs and whether it can be moved or needs to stay put, check the water supply and pressure feeding the room, and look at the floor and wall build-up to establish what's underneath the surfaces you can see. We also check access — door widths, staircases, lift availability in an apartment block, and how materials will move in and waste will move out — because that affects both the practicality of the work and, in some cases, the fittings you can realistically choose. By the end of the survey you get a written scope and a firm quote, not a ballpark figure that moves once work starts. We don't ask for a deposit to book the survey conversation itself; it's a paid, fixed-fee visit precisely so that the advice you get is based on your actual property, not a generic estimate drawn from somewhere else in the town.

sections.heading: What that looks like in a typical Maidenhead property
sections.body: Maidenhead's position on the Thames has shaped much of its more prestigious housing — larger detached properties along and near the river, some period, some built more recently, generally sitting on generous plots that give more freedom over bathroom layout than a terraced property allows. In one of these riverside houses, a survey often finds more usable floor area and fewer structural constraints on repositioning a waste run or widening a doorway for level access, though we still confirm floor loading and joist spacing properly rather than assuming the larger plot settles the question on its own. Away from the river, the town has a substantial core of Victorian and Edwardian housing, where original floor joists, period features and solid masonry walls are more often the deciding factors, plus extensive post-war and modern suburban development, where we're usually confirming what a previous owner has already boxed in. In the newer town-centre apartment schemes, the survey looks quite different again — shared waste stacks, restricted floor build-up, and sometimes a managing agent's conditions on what work can be carried out and when, all of which we check before a quote is written. Maidenhead sits close to Windsor, Eton and Twyford, and while each of those towns has its own character, the breadth of construction types we work with inside Maidenhead itself is wide enough that the survey genuinely has to look at your specific property rather than leaning on assumptions from elsewhere.

sections.heading: Booking your survey
sections.body: If you're planning a bathroom installation in Maidenhead, the survey is the sensible first step whether you already have a design in mind or you're still working out what's possible in the space. We'll come to the property, take the measurements and checks above, and talk through what you're hoping to achieve — whether that's a full reconfiguration, a wet room conversion, or simply replacing an existing layout with a higher specification. You'll leave the visit with a clear, written scope and a fixed quote for the installation, so you can compare it properly against anything else you're considering, without having to guess at what extra costs might appear later. We fit only — the survey covers what we need to install your bathroom to the specification you've chosen, and we work from your own supplied products or alongside your showroom or designer, whether that's for a riverside house, a Victorian terrace, or a town-centre flat.

faqs.q: Does the £125 survey fee come off the final price?
faqs.a: Yes. The £125 is a fixed fee for the visit itself, and it's deducted from your total project cost if you go ahead with an installation through us.

faqs.q: Do you survey Maidenhead apartments as well as houses?
faqs.a: Yes. Maidenhead has newer town-centre apartment schemes alongside its houses, and the survey for a flat covers the same ground as for a house — plus checking things specific to apartments, such as shared waste stacks, restricted floor build-up and any managing agent conditions on the work.

faqs.q: Does a riverside property near Maidenhead cost less to adapt at survey stage?
faqs.a: Riverside properties on generous plots often do give us more layout freedom than a terraced house, because relocating a waste run or widening a doorway is less likely to hit structural limits. We still confirm floor loading, joist spacing and waste position properly at survey rather than assuming the plot size settles it.

faqs.q: What happens if the survey finds a problem with the waste run or access?
faqs.a: We tell you at the survey, not partway through the job. If a waste run needs moving or a doorway needs widening for level access, that's scoped and priced into the written quote you receive, so there are no surprises once fitting starts.

faqs.q: Do I need a design ready before you survey my Maidenhead property?
faqs.a: No. Some of the Maidenhead properties we survey already have a finalised showroom or designer plan, and others are still at the idea stage. Either way, we measure the room, check waste and supply, and confirm what's structurally possible before any quote is written.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Maidenhead bathroom survey page, depicting the pre-installation measuring visit in a larger riverside-area property. Subject and action: a tape measure pulled taut across a section of exposed original floorboards beside a lifted section of subfloor, a spirit level laid flat across the gap, and an open clipboard with a hand-sketched floor plan propped against a roll of dust sheeting, as though a surveyor has just finished checking the joist line and stepped back. Setting and work-stage: a part-stripped ground-floor bathroom inside a substantial older house near the Thames on the edge of Maidenhead, early morning, cool daylight entering through a tall sash window with the curtains still drawn back from the night before. Composition: three-quarter angle from just inside the doorway, the exposed floorboards and tape measure filling the lower-left foreground, the sash window and a stack of folded dust sheets receding into the right background. Light and materials: aged original floorboards with visible grain and old nail holes, a section of exposed lime-plastered brick on the far wall, a single brushed bronze towel rail already fixed near the window from the previous fit-out, cool early-morning daylight mixing unevenly with a battery worklight propped on the floor. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on fixtures; no LED strip lighting anywhere in the frame; no catalog-symmetrical staging; no single uniform gold colour wash, light should fall unevenly across the room; no hanging plants, florals or styled candles; no running water; no uniform hyper-gloss, floorboards and masonry should show natural, varied sheen and believable wear.
image.heroAlt: A tape measure and spirit level laid across lifted original floorboards during a bathroom survey in a riverside-area Maidenhead house, exposed brick and a fixed brushed bronze towel rail visible under early-morning window light.
